items.title: Orrin Keepnews interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: like Symphony Sid in New York, like Sid McCoy in Chicago

ctx.x: Well the one record too that was from right here in San Francisco I believe, where you had the idea to keep his crowd talk on the record.

Well that was part of the first live date that we did with him and it became a signature thing. That was the first breakthrough record and the first hit record that I ever had, actually, The Cannonball Adderley Quintet in San Francisco was “Live at the Jazz Workshop,” which was for many years a famous jazz club in this town. And that was actually, like all good hit albums, was propelled by one song really. It had Bobby Timmons’ “This Here” which became an incredibly well put — it was funny, that was about a…

middle of the night, you could hear them forever. I think if you were being played by Symphony Sid in New York and by Sid McCoy out of WCFL I guess in Chicago, you could be heard practically everywhere. And these guys loved long numbers because they could then take a break, have a sandwich, go to the bathroom, whatever. I mean they loved twelve minute tunes. So the juxtaposition worked very well indeed. And that was I guess if my first artistic break was Monk, my second and my first commercial break was the…
